name: StayingAPI
tagline: Live availability, search and price across Airbnb, Booking.com, Vrbo and Google Hotels in one schema.

pricing.basis: starts free with 300 credits, failed and empty calls cost 0
pricing.notes: Subscription credits reset monthly; top-ups valid 30+ days.

verdictSummary: The booking platforms ship no usable public API on purpose, and they defend hard against scrapers. A single-platform personal scraper is a weekend hack that works until Airbnb or Booking rotate their defenses, which is often. The product is four hostile targets kept live behind one schema, with failed calls free because failure is the normal state of scraping these sites. Reproducing one platform badly is possible; reproducing the unified, durable, unblocked pipe across all four is the moat.
coreLoopDIY: Scrape one booking site's search results for availability and nightly price on given dates.
diyTimeEstimate: a weekend for one fragile platform
requirements: constant maintenance as each platform changes its defenses
whatYouLose: coverage across Airbnb, Booking.com, Vrbo and Google Hotels instead of one
one normalized schema instead of four brittle parsers
staying unblocked against platforms that actively fight scraping
the calls that fail silently on your side but not theirs
any reliability the day a platform ships new anti-bot measures
whyPeopleStillPay: Scraping one hostile booking site is a science project; keeping four of them live and normalized, indefinitely, through every defense update, is a full-time operation. You are paying for the four brittle pipes you do not want to own and the schema that hides their differences.
notes: One platform is a weekend hack; four kept unblocked forever is the product.
prompt: Build a FastAPI service that returns nightly availability and price for one vacation-rental listing on a single platform. Stack: Python 3.11, FastAPI, httpx, selectolax, uvicorn, no database. Endpoint: GET /quote?url=and checkIn=and checkOut= fetches the public listing page and returns JSON { available: bool, nightlyPrice, currency, source }. Use a real browser User-Agent, treat a blocked fetch as available=null with a clear reason, and never 500. Read an optional comma-separated PROXIES env var and rotate per request. Include /health, a README, and a .env.example, and state plainly in the README that this covers one platform, breaks under that platform's anti-bot defenses, and does not provide a unified cross-platform schema. Deliberately out of scope: more than one platform, a proxy pool you do not own, and login-gated data.
